title: Predictive auto-fit and accessible resize affordance for virtual table
creator: Asha Reddy
description: Introduce a predictive auto-fit column algorithm and a keyboard-first, screen-reader-friendly resize affordance for the virtualized table component. Goal: reduce manual fiddling, avoid layout jitter from measuring offscreen columns, and ensure resizing is discoverable and usable for keyboard and assistive tech users.
background: Current virtualized table only exposes a grab handle that requires precise pointer targeting. Double-click auto-fit is not supported consistently because many columns are not measured while virtualized. Teams have reported layout jumpiness when naive measuring runs, and platform QA flagged poor keyboard + screen reader support for resizing.
proposal: 1) Auto-fit heuristic: use a light-weight sampling pass that computes representative content widths for each column group (header, first N visible rows, and a small offscreen sample) to populate a predictive width cache. Auto-fit action (double-click header divider or context action) will compute a suggested width from the cache and animate to that size.
tradeoffs:
- Sampling avoids full measurement work but may misestimate for skewed rows (very long single cell). We will surface a subtle overflow indicator for corner cases.
- Prefilling widths reduces layout shift but adds complexity in cache invalidation (on data change, column visibility change, font scaling). Invalidation policy will be conservative: invalidate on row delta > 10% or on column schema change.
- Accessibility-first handles may feel slightly different visually; we prioritize keyboard affordance and ARIA announcements over custom pointer-only micro-interactions.
tasks: Design: produce annotated Figma components for header divider states (idle, hover, active, keyboard-focus, announced)
Engineering: ENG-43891 implement predictive width cache and sampling pass in runtime layer
Engineering: ENG-43902 add animation and safe layout update path to avoid jank during resize
Design: write copy for overflow indicator and accessible live region messages
QA: create regression suite covering virtualization + auto-fit + density modes
acceptance_criteria: Double-clicking a header divider triggers an auto-fit that uses cached widths and animates without causing visible layout jumping beyond the local column area
Keyboard: focusable divider handle can be adjusted with Arrow keys (small) and PageUp/PageDown (larger steps); Enter triggers auto-fit; Esc cancels
Screen reader announces: column name, current width, and instructions when divider receives focus; live region announces auto-fit completion
Sampling policy invalidates cache correctly on major data or schema changes (demonstrable test cases)
Works across density modes (compact, default, spacious) and respects design tokens for spacing and handle hit area
Performance: predictive sampling pass adds < 6ms p95 on large tables (50k rows virtualized) in our benchmark harness
design_notes:
- Use a circular 24px hit target centered on the divider for pointer, but show a 12px visual hairline to preserve compact column visuals.
- Provide a secondary 'Quick-fit' icon in header context menu for touch users where double-click isn't available.
- When a column contains long tokens (emails, long IDs) show a trailing '…' with tooltip on hover; quick-fit chooses width to fit the most common token length, not the max token, to avoid extremely wide columns.
- Tokens: introduce token 'table.resize.handle.hit' = 24px and 'table.resize.animation.duration' = 160ms in design tokens set.
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Initial research complete — measured current resize jitter on three sample apps. Identified main culprit: synchronous measuring of entire data window.
2026-02-27: Prototype created in Figma demonstrating keyboard flow and overflow indicator. Shared with PM and runtime eng for feedback.
2026-03-05: Sync with ENG runtime team; agreed on predictive width cache API shape and invalidation hooks. Engineering will spike sampling implementation (ENG-43891).
notes_for_engineers: Provide a non-blocking fallback when the predictive cache misses: fall back to existing fixed-min measurement and surface overflow indicator. Expose telemetry hooks: sample_count, cache_hit_ratio, average_resize_ms.
